direction: Refine the strict prefix-causal `score_bin` residual scoring toward a best-fit-dominant rule with a symmetric residual dead-zone: prefer bins whose post-placement residual is near 0 (exact fit) or near w (perfect complementary pairing), and strongly penalize mid-range fragment residuals, while keeping bin-open decisions strictly causal (only observe items already seen, never look ahead).

operations.mechanism: Round 1 gave a single solver at mean objective 27.8333 (SBS=VBS, i.e. no complementary alternative exists yet), and the archive's weakest regimes are the small/medium sizes (50, 100) where VBS relative gaps are most negative — these are the instances where fragmentation from a plain fill-after-placement score hurts most, since a wrong early bin choice propagates over the whole prefix. KB island ablations show the dead-zone/exp-utilization family (B1) plus closing bonuses (B16, B50) beat plain Best Fit on Weibull and BPPLib streams, and all are dimensionless ratio formulas with 0.00% drift under 10x capacity scaling. So the plan is to keep the allowed template and `none` postprocess, and let the inner EoH evolution search the hook space around Best-Fit + residual dead-zone + 85-90% close bonus, which is a pure score_bin change that cannot break prefix-causality or the 500 ms budget (round-1 solve mean was only 1.2 ms, leaving large headroom).

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: For online bin packing with strict prefix-causal scoring (irrevocable placement, no future item information), the dominant driver of bin count is residual fragmentation: a score_bin that minimizes the arithmetic residual together with a dead-zone penalty on mid-range residuals (r in (eps, w-eps)) will match or beat pure Best Fit on dev_24, because it both packs tightly now and preserves a residual distribution that stays size-compatible with the empirical item-size distribution. Indexing the penalty by a scale-free ratio r/w keeps it robust to bin-capacity shifts (no 10x capacity drift), and an exponential closing bonus once a bin exceeds ~90% utilization should convert nearly-full bins into closed bins sooner.
